text: When you get an E12 high temperature alert above 80°C on M1 (Tab Laser Welding Cell), nine times out of ten it is weld spatter buildup on the protective optics window. Even if the chiller looks fine, a contaminated cover glass absorbs laser energy and heats the head fast. Best bet is to inspect and swap the protective optics window first.

We have seen a few false positives on the vibration sensor for M1 right after a sensor swap or fixture changeout. Persistent E13 vibration alerts above 50 mm/s usually point to loose clamping fixture bolts or linear stage bearing wear on the welding gantry.

Last quarter we had repeated E12 high-temp alerts on the Tab Laser Welding Cell during long EV module runs. We traced it to an intermittent coolant blockage in the laser head return line—the flexible chiller tubing was kinking during rapid gantry moves. Replacing the coolant tubing and adding a support bracket fixed it.

One challenge with E13 vibration alerts on M1 is that normal high-speed tab welding brings gantry vibration up to 38–44 mm/s. Anything sustained above 50 mm/s means we need to check the clamping fixture torque and linear stage bearings against recent tooling swaps.

We trained new hires to always inspect both the focusing lens assembly and the protective optics window whenever E12 triggers, and to check the clamping fixture bolts if E13 triggers. Visual inspection catches micro-cracks and spatter early before weld quality degrades.
